title: Base change of a Noetherian local algebra along a finite purely inseparable extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $k'/k$ a finite purely inseparable field extension [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] [def-pc-field-extension], of degree $d=[k':k]=\dim_kk'$, and $(A,\mathfrak m,K)$ a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring (a commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, residue field $K=A/\mathfrak m$) which is a $k$-algebra. Put $A'=A\otimes_kk'$, an $A$-algebra via $a\mapsto a\otimes1$. Then: (1) $A'$ is a free $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-free-module] of rank $d$, in particular $A'$ is a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] (i.e. $A\to A'$ is finite) and $A\to A'$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and $A'$ is Noetherian; (2) $A'$ is a local ring, and its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m'$ is the only prime ideal of $A'$ containing $\mathfrak mA'$; (3) the residue field $K'=A'/\mathfrak m'$ is a finite field extension of $K$ (via $K=A/\mathfrak m\to A'/\mathfrak m'$), and there is an isomorphism of rings $A'/\mathfrak mA'\cong K\otimes_kk'$, $(a\otimes x)\bmod\mathfrak mA'\mapsto\bar a\otimes x$, compatible with the maps from $A$; in particular $A'/\mathfrak mA'$ is a $K$-algebra of dimension $d$ over $K$.

proof.text: *Clause (1).* Let $b_1,\dots,b_d$ be a $k$-basis of $k'$ ($k'/k$ finite [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-free-base-change-tower] to the ring maps $k\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}k\to A$ and the $k$-module $M=k'$: $k'\otimes_kk\cong k'$ is free over $k$ with basis $b_j\otimes1$, hence $k'\otimes_kA$ is a free $A$-module with basis $b_1\otimes1,\dots,b_d\otimes1$. The swap $k'\otimes_kA\to A\otimes_kk'$, $x\otimes a\mapsto a\otimes x$, is an $A$-linear isomorphism, so $A'$ is free over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module] with basis $1\otimes b_1,\dots,1\otimes b_d$, of rank $d$. A free module with a finite basis is finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], so $A\to A'$ is finite. A free module is flat [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat], so $A\to A'$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. As $A$ is Noetherian and $A'$ is a finitely generated $A$-module, $A'$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian]. Finally $A\ne0$ and $d\ge1$, so $A'\ne0$.

proof.text: *The closed fibre.* By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] for $A\to A'$ and $I=\mathfrak m$, $A'/\mathfrak mA'\cong A'\otimes_A(A/\mathfrak m)=A'\otimes_AK$ as $A'$-algebras, $b\bmod\mathfrak mA'\mapsto b\otimes1$. The swap $A'\otimes_AK\cong K\otimes_A(A\otimes_kk')$ is a ring isomorphism, and [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] (with $R=k$, $S=A$, $B=k'$ and the $A$-algebra $K$) gives the $K$-algebra isomorphism $K\otimes_A(A\otimes_kk')\cong K\otimes_kk'$, $c\otimes(a\otimes x)\mapsto\bar ac\otimes x$. The composite $\psi:A'/\mathfrak mA'\to K\otimes_kk'$ is a ring isomorphism with $(a\otimes x)\bmod\mathfrak mA'\mapsto\bar a\otimes x$; it is compatible with the maps from $A$ ($a\mapsto\bar a\otimes1$ on both sides), so it is $K$-linear for the $K=A/\mathfrak m$-algebra structure of $A'/\mathfrak mA'$ induced by $A\to A'$. Since $K$ is a field and a $k$-algebra, $K/k$ is a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], and by [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension] the elements $b_j\otimes1$ form a $K$-basis of $k'\otimes_kK\cong K\otimes_kk'$; so $\dim_K(K\otimes_kk')=d\ge1$, in particular $K\otimes_kk'\ne0$ and the ring map $K\to K\otimes_kk'$, $c\mapsto c\otimes1$, is injective (its kernel is a proper ideal of the field $K$).

proof.text: *Every element of $B=K\otimes_kk'$ is a unit or nilpotent.* If $k$ has characteristic $0$, then $k'=k$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], so $B\cong K$ is a field and the claim holds. Let $k$ have characteristic $p>0$; then $p\cdot1=0$ in the $k$-algebras $k'$ and $B$. Let $z=\sum_{i=1}^nc_i\otimes x_i\in B$ ($c_i\in K$, $x_i\in k'$). Each $x_i$ has $x_i^{p^{e_i}}\in k$ for some $e_i\ge0$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]; put $e=\max_ie_i$, $q=p^e$; then $x_i^q=(x_i^{p^{e_i}})^{p^{e-e_i}}\in k$. The $e$-fold Frobenius $F_B^e:y\mapsto y^q$ is a ring endomorphism of $B$ [def-weil-ring-frobenius], so $z^q=\sum_ic_i^q\otimes x_i^q=\sum_ic_i^qx_i^q\otimes1=c\otimes1$ with $c=\sum_ic_i^qx_i^q\in K$ (moving the scalars $x_i^q\in k$ across $\otimes_k$). If $c=0$ then $z^q=0$ and $z$ is nilpotent. If $c\ne0$, then $c\otimes1$ is a unit of $B$ with inverse $c^{-1}\otimes1$, so $z\cdot(z^{q-1}(c^{-1}\otimes1))=1$ and $z$ is a unit.

proof.text: *$B$ is local with unique prime $N$, the nilradical.* Let $N\subseteq B$ be the set of nilpotent elements; it is an ideal (if $x^a=0=y^b$ then $(x+y)^{a+b}=0$ by the binomial formula, and $(rx)^a=0$). $B\ne0$ (step 2), so $1\notin N$ and $N$ is a proper ideal. By step 3 every element outside $N$ is a unit, so every proper ideal of $B$ (which contains no unit) lies in $N$; hence $N$ is the unique maximal ideal and $B/N$ is a field. Every prime ideal $P$ of $B$ contains $N$ ($x^a=0\in P$ implies $x\in P$) and is proper, so $P=N$: $N$ is the only prime ideal of $B$.

proof.text: *Clause (2).* Let $\pi:A'\to A'/\mathfrak mA'$ be the quotient map and $\mathfrak m'=\pi^{-1}(\psi^{-1}(N))$ with $\psi$ of step 2. Prime ideals of $A'$ containing $\mathfrak mA'$ correspond bijectively, by $P\mapsto\psi(\pi(P))$, to prime ideals of $A'/\mathfrak mA'\cong B$ (correspondence theorem for the surjection $\pi$ and the isomorphism $\psi$); by step 4 there is exactly one, so $\mathfrak m'$ is the only prime of $A'$ containing $\mathfrak mA'$, and $A'/\mathfrak m'\cong B/N$ is a field, so $\mathfrak m'$ is maximal. Conversely, $A'$ is a finitely generated module over the local ring $A$ (step 1), so every maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $A'$ contains $\mathfrak mA'$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-local-radical]; being prime, $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m'$. Hence $\mathfrak m'$ is the unique maximal ideal and $A'$ is a local ring.

proof.text: *Clause (3).* The isomorphism $A'/\mathfrak mA'\cong K\otimes_kk'$ with $\dim_K=d$ is step 2. The surjection $A'/\mathfrak mA'\to A'/\mathfrak m'=K'$ (as $\mathfrak mA'\subseteq\mathfrak m'$) is $K$-linear, so $K'$ is spanned over $K$ by the images of $d$ basis vectors and $\dim_KK'\le d<\infty$; $K'$ is a field (step 5) and $K\to K'$ is a ring map of fields, injective, so $K'/K$ is a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension].
